narrative: Material PL1__MCE82DD5 exhibits high-volume, near-continuous demand (mean 618 units/day, CV 0.53) with a statistically significant upward trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly volatile (CV 1.29), with most deliveries same-day but occasional multi-day delays driving safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 5,554 units and a safety stock of 1,130 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level while reducing annual ordering frequency from ~445 to ~28 cycles, yielding an estimated 85% reduction in total inventory costs.
warnings: Volatile lead times detected (CV = 1.29) — monitor supplier delivery performance closely.
Significant upward demand trend detected (slope +2.14 units/day, p < 0.001) — review mean demand parameters quarterly.
SAP safety lead time (3.5 days) exceeds empirically recommended value (1.83 days) — recommend reduction.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (97% non-zero days) and high-volume, making continuous-review appropriate. The EOQ formula provides the cost-minimising order quantity, and the reorder point incorporates both average lead-time demand and a safety stock buffer against lead-time volatility. The MOQ (347) is well below the EOQ (5,554), so the EOQ dominates and no MOQ tension exists.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (6,709 units) is not binding: SS (1,130) + OQ (5,554) = 6,684 < 6,709. Margin is only 25 units; any upward revision to safety stock (e.g., due to demand trend acceleration) could require a corresponding reduction in order quantity.
